cohort: The cohort consisted of birthing people in Louisiana with singleton live births between 2016 and 2022, categorized by their relationship type (same-sex or different-sex) and race/ethnicity.
finding: Sexual orientation-related disparities in obstetric and perinatal outcomes exist across and within racial/ethnic groups among birthing people in Louisiana, with those in same-sex relationships generally experiencing higher risks for certain adverse outcomes, particularly when intersecting with racial/ethnic identity.
mod_finding: Birthing people in same-sex relationships were less likely to have spontaneous labor compared with those in different-sex relationships.
